newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chronology - a bad year in space for Russia's Mir.
newsitem.headline: Chronology - a bad year in space for Russia's Mir.

text.p: When a tired crewman pulled out a cable and plunged Russia's Mir space station into crisis on Thursday it was the latest in a jinx-like string of mishaps to hit the world's only orbital laboratory this year.
They have raised doubts about its future and that of Russian cooperation in space with the United States and other nations.
"Accidents have happened before," Russia's NTV commercial television commented. "But this year Mir can perhaps claim a line or two in the Guinness Book of Records."
Following is a brief chronology of this year's malfunctions on board the station first launched in 1985:

Feb 24 - Fire breaks out when comonauts try to change an air filter. German Reinhold Ewald, American Jerry Linenger and Russians Vasily Tsibliyev, Alexander Lazutkin, Alexander Koleri and Valery Korzun are on board. The crew have to spend sometime in gas masks after fumes were released during the incident.
March 6 - Progress cargo craft fails to dock and is dumped.
March 7 - Oxygen supply generator fails, forcing crew to use backup chemical system. They again spend time in gas masks.
April 4 - Mir develops leak in cooling system, briefly knocking out device used to maintain breathable air on board.

June 25 - Another Progress hits Mir during practice docking, puncturing the Spektr module, writing off one solar battery and forcing crew to cut cables to three others. Electric power supply cut by up to half. British-born NASA astronaut Michael Foale, Lazutkin and Tsibliyev on board. Officials will neither confirm nor deny collision was caused by mistake by Tsibliyev.
July 3 - Gyroscopic guidance devices that should keep remaining solar panels lined up on the Sun fail. Mir's orientaton is adjusted by firing rocket engines.
July 5 - Cosmonauts report thumping sounds and see something leaking from the holed Spektr module. Officials say they don't know what it was but insist it was not fuel.
July 14 - Commander Tsibliyev reports heart palpitation.

July 16 - Medical commission puts Tsibliyev on sedatives and heart pills and bars him from taking part in repairs to Spektr solar panel cables. Foale is set to step in alongside engineer Lazutkin. Job is put back from around July 18 to around July 24.

July 17 - One of the crew mistakenly pulls out a vital computer cable prompting massive power failure aboard the ship. Cosmonauts ordered to continue training for repairs but officials say some new delay seems likely.
